title: Python SDK: unified streaming sink + resume hooks for chat completions
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem summary: Users building streaming chat integrations with the Python SDK are facing three recurring pain points: 1) scattered callback shapes for incremental tokens vs structured events, 2) lack of a small, composable contract for checkpoint/resume semantics (needed for flaky networks and long-lived conversations), and 3) unclear retry/idempotency behavior when applying partial outputs to user state.

This ticket proposes a lightweight "unified streaming sink" API and resume hooks that: (a) normalize event shapes (start, delta, tool_call, structured_output, end, error, meta), (b) expose a checkpoint/resume contract with user-provided idempotency keys and explicit boundaries, and (c) specify retry semantics with guidance and helpers for common app patterns (UI streaming, transcript persistence, server-side reruns). The goal is ergonomic defaults plus explicit escape hatches for advanced producers/consumers.
acceptance_criteria: API spec document checked into docs/ with examples for 3 patterns: live UI, server-side transcript writer, resumable background worker
Unit tests covering sink callbacks, checkpoint serialization, and retry idempotency helpers (>=80% coverage for new modules)
A small demo app in examples/py demonstrating resume after network interruption and at-least-once delivery handling
Design review approval from SDK/Developer Experience and Reliability teams
No breaking changes to existing Python streaming public helpers (backwards-compatible wrappers provided if signatures change)
design_notes: Core abstraction: StreamingSink (protocol) with methods: on_event(event_type: str, payload: str, meta: str) -> Optional[Checkpoint]; checkpoint is an opaque string serializable by user
Events: 'session_start' (meta), 'token_delta' (raw text chunk), 'structured_delta' (json schema string), 'tool_call' (json string), 'session_end' (meta), 'error' (meta)

Checkpoint model: stable opaque string produced by SDK or user-provided serializer. Checkpoint indicates a replay-safe boundary: replays after checkpoint MUST be idempotent to user state when applying deltas. SDK will provide a helper serializer that includes sequence index, request_id, and partial-kv-cache-hash

Retry semantics: SDK guarantees at-least-once delivery of events. It will provide an IdempotentApplier helper with simple APIs: try_apply(checkpoint) -> bool and apply_delta(delta, checkpoint) -> bool. Users can opt into exactly-once techniques by using application-level dedupe keys derived from checkpoint

Backpressure/backoff: sink can return control signals to the SDK: CONTINUE / PAUSE_FOR(s) / STOP. Default consumer will buffer up to N tokens (configurable) and apply PAUSE if processing lag exceeds threshold

Ergonomic sync/async parity: same sink contract available for both sync and async clients. Provide adapters: SyncSinkWrapper -> async compatible via threadpool, AsyncSinkWrapper -> sync by running event loop in background thread
API naming: keep 'on_event' as minimalist surface. Provide high-level convenience wrapper 'StreamConsumer' that accepts callbacks: on_token, on_structured, on_end, on_error for quick migration
implementation_plan: Week 1: Draft API spec in PRD + unit-test skeletons. Prototype unified sink as an internal module and wire to current streaming codepath (non-breaking toggle flag)
Week 2: Implement checkpoint serializer & IdempotentApplier helper. Add buffer/backpressure controls and expose config knobs via client.StreamOptions
Week 3: Build high-level wrappers (StreamConsumer) and adapters for sync/async parity. Add demo example and docs
Week 4: Integration tests with network interruption simulation. Run design review and reliability runbook review. Prepare rollout plan with feature flag behind 'stream_unified_sink'
Post-merge: Monitor metrics for streaming error/retry rates and customer support tickets for one week, iterate based on feedback
risks: Behavioral compatibility: risk of breaking user callbacks if we change the existing streaming event shapes. Mitigation: provide backward-compatible compatibility layer and opt-in flag
Checkpoint leakage: treating checkpoint as opaque string relies on users not mutating it; provide strong docs and example serializations
Performance: additional buffering and checkpoint operations could add latency. Mitigation: benchmark extra allocations and make helper serializer C-optimized in later iteration
Complexity for users: too many knobs might confuse adopters. Mitigation: ship sensible defaults and a single convenience wrapper for common patterns
dependencies_notes: Relies on existing stream router and retry helpers in ENG-7421 and ENG-17109 for ingress/backoff primitives
Coordination with Console telemetry team (ENG-127340) to surface streaming-level metrics (bytes/sec, avg-latency-per-token) for monitoring
Will reference design assets in drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/py-streaming-ergonomics/spec-v1 (placeholder link)
test_plan: Unit tests: simulate SSE/websocket streaming events, assert checkpoint produced and consumed correctly
Integration: run an end-to-end example where a client receives 120s of tokens, simulates a TCP drop at 35s, resumes using checkpoint and verifies deduplication
Property tests: fuzz deltas and ensure IdempotentApplier prevents duplicate inserts given repeated replay
Load test: 1000 concurrent small streams to ensure buffer limits and backpressure signals behave under contention
notes: Review feedback from internal SDK sync (2026-03-05): prefer minimal 'on_event' surface to reduce cognitive load; add clear examples for common UI patterns
Open question: should checkpoints include model KV cache fingerprint? (affects replay semantics for streaming autocompletion chains). We'll prototype with optional kv_hash field in serializer
Follow-up: create a short migration guide for existing streaming users to adopt the convenience wrapper without reworking app code
